exploration.title: Light Bending Studio
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Aim a beam, swap materials and discover when light bends or reflects.
exploration.question: What happens when light reaches a different material?
exploration.explanation: Reflection sends light back into its first material. Refraction can bend light as it crosses into a material where it travels at a different speed. Measure angles from the normal: the line at right angles to the surface. From air into water, a slanting ray bends toward the normal. This single-color ray model leaves out changes in brightness and the separation of colors.

experiments.title: Find total internal reflection
experiments.instruction: Predict whether a transmitted ray remains for glass to air above 42°. Choose a prediction, then Test glass to air at 43°. Compare 40° and 43° with materials fixed.
experiments.observe: The transmitted ray disappears above the critical angle. Explain why the direction from higher to lower refractive index matters.

experiments.title: Reverse the materials
experiments.instruction: Predict whether air to glass can produce total internal reflection. Swap materials and compare at the same angle. Then set both indices equal.
experiments.observe: The transmitted ray persists from air to glass; equal indices show no reflected branch or bending. Explain both observations using refractive index.

exploration.misconception: Total internal reflection is possible only from a higher to a lower refractive index, above the critical angle. It does not happen at every boundary.
